speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The purpose of this prohibition is to deter would-be attackers from carrying out pre-attack surveys of their targets.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, while many Protected Areas or Places have "No Photography" signs outside, authorised officers are not able to stop persons from taking photos.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the ground, the authorised officers will have to exercise some judgement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If photos were taken inadvertently, they would typically warn and ask the person to delete the photos.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Further action would be taken if the person does not comply, or if there are security reasons to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Bill will limit the availability of more recent and detailed photographs of Protected Areas and Places.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such photos can threaten public safety and security by facilitating the planning of attacks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Making it clear that unauthorised photography is prohibited will also have a deterrent effect, allowing security resources to focus on areas that are more likely to be a real threat.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how many people have been charged or warned against taking photographs or videos of Protected Areas and Places, and how awareness will be increased.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Currently, because this is not an offence – though some of our Protected Areas and Places like our checkpoints have rules to disallow it – no one has committed an offence since it is not an offence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Sylvia Lim had asked what were the reasons for the increase in fines under Part 3.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The PAPPA has not been amended since 1959.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Well, it is benchmarked to similar and more recent offences, such as those in the Public Order Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, remaining in the special event area without authorisation and contravention of move-on orders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those are the benchmarks that have been looked at.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh spoke about the need for other counterterrorism efforts to complement infrastructure protection.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I share his views that we need to step up on all fronts, including regional cooperation and strengthening religious harmony which we will debate in Mr Christopher de Souza's Motion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Melvin Yong mentioned the importance of preparing members of the staff and public so that they know how to respond in the event of emergencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Just last week, Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean spoke about the important role of the corporate sector.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Businesses can help raise the preparedness of their workers, for example, by briefing employees on emergency escape routes and places to hide, and equipping them with firefighting, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)/automated external defibrillator (AED) as well as first-aid skills.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The SGSecure Guide for Workplaces was also launched recently and will be made available to all companies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We urge all companies to study the guide and take steps to raise preparedness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for Mr Melvin Yong's suggestion on coordinated evacuation plans, I think he talked about sector level plans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police and the Singapore Civil Defence Force conduct annual exercises with the Watch group members to enhance joint responses to crises and incidents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some of these exercises are conducted with a cluster of buildings located in the same area.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira, and I believe Ms Sylvia Lim, spoke about protecting hospitals since they provide essential services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The efforts include building security measures, patrols by the Police, and also engagement through the Safety and Security Watch Group scheme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Each hospital has put in place preventive security measures, physical security operations and contingency plans to deal with different scenarios, including terrorist incidents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the support of the House, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.10 pm until 4.30 pm.
